newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner consortium wins Australian oil ship deal.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner consortium wins Australian oil ship deal.

text.p: Shipbuilding and engineeering group Kvaerner ASA confirmed on Friday it and Dutch group IHC Caland NV had been awarded a turnkey contract for the world's largest production barge by Australian oil company Woodside Offshore Petroleum.
The contract, worth about $420 million, was awarded to Kvaerner subsiaidary Kvaerner Engineering in Oslo and Swiss-based Single Buoy Moorings Inc (SBM), a member of the IHC Caland group.

Kvaerner will provide the topsides for the production barge and SBM the large diameter turret mooring and fluid transfer system. The contract embraces design, procurement, fabrication, supervision, commissioning and start up of the production vessel.
It also covers planned and unplanned maintenance over the first three years of the field's operation phase with an option throughout the life of the field.
The contract for the vessel's hull was awarded earlier to Korea's Samsung Heavy Industries. This agreement will be included in the turnkey contract and managed by the consortium.
The vessel is due to begin producing crude from the Laminaria and Corallina oilfields in the Timor Sea off northwest Australia at the end of 1998 or in early 1999.
It will operate in a water depth of around 365 metres and will have a production capacity of roughly 170,000 barrels per day of oil and will be able to store 1.4 million barrels.
Licensees on the Laminaria field are Woodside, the operator with 50 percent and Shell Australia and BHP Petroleum with 25 percent each.
